name: Example: Improper Integrals Involving Arctangent Using the First Result
worked_solution:
First, let's recall the following result:

$$
\int \dfrac{1}{1+(kx)^2} \, \textrm dx = \dfrac{1}{k} \arctan \left(kx \right) + C
$$

We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to\infty.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1/4}^{\infty }\frac{2}{1+16{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{-1/4}^{a}\frac{1}{1+16{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{-1/4}^{a}\frac{1}{1+(4x)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4x)]}_{-1/4}^{a} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4a)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4a)]-(-\frac{\pi }{4})) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4a)]+\frac{\pi }{4})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\arctan{(4x)},$ shown in the graph below:

- $\lim\limits_{x \to -\infty} \left[\arctan{(4x)}\right] = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

- $\lim\limits_{x \to \infty} \left[\arctan{(4x)}\right] = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14039465/assets/9a7272f8bc8d0eba3e5bfc38e843cd02db3f3eb7b51e77b95b2efd61034890b6.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1/4}^{\infty }\frac{2}{1+16{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(4a)]+\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
